# What fix was validated through mock, real machine and merged PR testing for multi-hardware, asynchronous read/write due to jitter?

> **Current answer:** PR #2091 no longer only uses a fixed 0.99 threshold to determine if a frequency is too frequent, but compares the timing error of execution in the current cycle versus the next cycle after a controller-manager period. The author tested this across multiple frequencies, mock components, and UR16e+KR50 real machines; read/write skips were reduced to below 0.01%. This PR has been merged. Divisional frequencies still need to be quantized, and acceptance must be based on the target combination.

## Key terms

- Read/write rate (rw_rate) (读写频率)
- Controller-manager update rate (控制管理器更新率)
- Periodicity jitter (周期抖动)
- Skipped cycle (跳过周期)

## Problem and symptoms

- Why does hardware with rw_rate=250 on controller-manager 500 Hz occasionally skip every three cycles? How to fix it?
- Slow hardware expects ~4 ms call, but frequently jumps to ~6 ms, causing motion stutter.
- In a 500-second trace, write over 5 ms is 20.5%, and read is 0.74%.

## Environment

- Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS; ROS 2 Jazzy; ros2_control source build; UR16e 500 Hz, KUKA KR50 250 Hz; additional mock testing.

## Priority diagnostics

- Record read/write cycle distribution, not just average frequency.
- Compare reduction of fixed thresholds with timing-error-based scheduling.
- Cover 100/150/250/333 Hz and controller-manager 500/1000 Hz.

## Possible causes

- Original logic only checked if a call was too frequent; fast interfaces can cause slow interfaces to fall below 0.99 threshold and skip one cycle.

## Attempts

- The 0.98 and 0.97 thresholds were reduced to only reduce skips; the author now compares the timing error of execution in the current cycle versus the next cycle.
- Initial mock and multi-frequency testing, followed by testing on UR16e+KR50 real machine.

## Effective fixes

- Use the rw_rate timing-error selection logic from merged PR #2091.

## Result

- Real machine trace shows read/write skips below 0.01%; PR #2091 has been reviewed, tested and merged.

## Limitations

- At 150 Hz relative to 500/1000 Hz, the thread display shows actual frequency quantized to 166.66 or 142.87 Hz; cannot promise exact hit for any target frequency.
- The author believes the remaining few skips may be related to the RT/low-latency kernel test environment, but this is their judgment, not an independent conclusion.

## Safety notes

- After multi-hardware system upgrade, check each interface's cycle distribution and missed cycles in power-off or low-speed mode.

## Applicability boundary

- ROS 2 Jazzy, ros2_control multi-hardware components where rw_rate is below controller-manager update rate.
